overallAssessment: You're a VP of Operations at a B2B security SaaS trying to break into a marketplace strategy role at Webflow. While you have strong operational chops, you lack the critical marketplace-specific experience, SQL proficiency, and product strategy depth this role demands.

strengths.evidence: Led operations across 5 departments at SpiderOak, managed cross-functional teams, and drove 15% ARR growth
Built customer success org from scratch, implemented new systems (billing, support queue), and have hands-on technical experience with modern tools
Reduced time-to-hire by 50%, improved customer retention by 25%, cut support backlog by 80% - shows metrics orientation
Successfully led distributed teams at SpiderOak in fully remote environment, aligns with Webflow's remote-first culture

gaps.concern: No evidence of marketplace, creator economy, or multi-sided platform experience. This role is specifically about managing a marketplace ecosystem.
gaps.question: Have you worked with any marketplace platforms, creator economies, or managed relationships between buyers and sellers in any capacity?
gaps.userContext: Well, this hasn't been an explicit job that I've held for the past ten years. My wife and I have had a side hustle involving retail arbitrage. This has allowed us to dip our toes into all kinds of different things, from selling on various e-commerce platforms, setting up platforms like eBay, Shopify, and WooCommerce—two being part of creator economies. The creator economy involves selling things like books and templates. This has never progressed to the point where we were running a marketplace, but I have been involved in these areas and have end-user experience that has really helped me better understand how these marketplaces function and what makes a good one versus a bad one.

gaps.concern: Job explicitly requires SQL proficiency. Resume mentions 'SQL (Postgres)' in tools but no evidence of actual data analysis work or SQL-driven insights.
gaps.question: Can you describe a specific project where you wrote SQL queries to derive business insights? What was the complexity level?
gaps.userContext: Postgres and SQL queries have been a big part of my life at Spider Oak because of the way we run the master customer database. Everything from monthly finance queries to running user statistics involves writing queries, and this has become necessary due to the lack of documentation about the schema. This has become a constant part of my life, as I am one of the few people at the company who has learned enough to understand the database schema and write effective queries. This isn't a bullet point on my resume, but it could be, because I've spent so much time with this Postgres database. In the last few months, I've also worked on numerous side projects involving Postgres, and I've learned a lot about creating database schemas and working with databases to power various types of apps, almost always in a multi-tenant environment because of the kind of apps I was creating.

gaps.concern: While you were a product owner for CrossClave, there's limited evidence of strategic product work, pricing strategy, or experiment design.
gaps.question: Can you walk through a product strategy you developed from ideation through execution, including pricing decisions and experiment design?
gaps.userContext:
Crosslave is a great example of this. We came up with the idea for Crosslave, which was a B2B encrypted messaging and file storage solution that also had public sharing elements. We went from a product idea to a product MVP, and then I was in charge of the initiative to set up the e-commerce part. 

This involved finding out how to create the initial pricing tiers, modifying those tiers over time, and making sure that we had both the ability for customers to purchase through our e-commerce platform and to evaluate where in the funnel customers dropped off. 

This led to the consolidation of different product types and tiers; initially, we had several levels, but over time, we consolidated them into the most common product levels. This particular product didn't survive very long beyond the MVP due to a lack of development resources and a company pivot, but I was able to go through these early-stage growth experiences and learned a lot about product development and go-to-market strategies.

gaps.concern: Role requires building solutions with low/no-code tools. Your experience is more traditional engineering and DevOps focused.
gaps.question: Have you built any operational solutions using no-code platforms like Zapier, Airtable, or Webflow itself?
gaps.userContext: Webflow itself has become a huge part of what I do outside of Spider Oak. In fact, in the last couple of months, we've made a move because of how much I enjoy using Webflow. I've started an initiative inside SpiderOak to move from our current CMS to using Webflow itself. Outside of SpiderOak, I work with the American Jazz Museum, whose CMS runs on Webflow. I've learned a ton about integrations with Webflow and how to use various automation tools to connect with Webflow. Airtable and Zapier are old friends, as well as tools like n8n. I use these frequently in my own life, from Apple Shortcuts on my phone and iPad to Notion for different groups I participate in. Wherever I can create automations, I try to, and often that comes in the form of using no-code platforms.
